entries.proposition: The cohort is a parent-reported natural-history survey, cross-sectional with no longitudinal data; 48 individuals with 38 unique variants, 36 of them missense.
entries.snippet: Among the 48 participants, there were 38 unique KCNQ2 variants (36 missense, 1 in‐frame deletion, 1 frameshift).

entries.proposition: Seizure response to drugs is parent-reported as significant or complete reduction: 7 of 13 on carbamazepine, 13 of 17 on oxcarbazepine, 10 of 13 on phenytoin; the denominators are those who received each drug, with no control and no timing.
entries.snippet: Significant complete reduction of seizures in response to specific sodium channel blocking anti‐seizure medications was reported in 7 of 13 (54%) for carbamazepine, 13 of 17 (76%) for oxcarbazepine, and 10 of 13 (77%) for phenytoin.

entries.proposition: A good to excellent response to retigabine was reported in 3 of 4 individuals, and the variants of responders all responded to the drug in vitro.
entries.snippet: KCNQ2 variants associated with clinical responses to retigabine all showed significant in vitro responses to the drug
entries.anchor: Results, Correlation of variant function with clinical features

entries.proposition: The authors state that timing of antiseizure medication use was not captured, so the question of early seizure control and development cannot be addressed here.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, we had limited information about the timing of use of anti‐seizure medications in our study cohort.

entries.proposition: The authors cite earlier analyses showing a dissociation between ongoing seizures and severity of the non-seizure aspects of the disorder.
entries.snippet: Previous analyses demonstrated a dissociation between ongoing seizures and severity of the non‐seizure aspects of the disorder.

entries.proposition: Functional class was assigned by current density relative to wild type (severe loss below 25 percent, moderate loss 25 to 75, wild-type-like 75 to 125, gain above 125) in a heterologous cell line with the partner subunit, and the classification was done blind to phenotype.
entries.snippet: Importantly, functional studies and classifications of impact on channel function were conducted blind to the specific phenotypes.

entries.proposition: No single non-seizure feature was associated with functional class; the composite severity score was modestly higher in severe loss than in moderate loss (p 0.02, rho 0.32).
entries.snippet: While no single phenotypic feature was associated with variant function, there was a modestly higher PSS in those with SLOF (median = 2; IQR 1–3) versus LOF (median = 1; IQR 1–2.5) variants (Mann–Whitney U yielded p = 0.02; Spearman rho coefficient = 0.32, p = 0.02)

entries.proposition: The lower proportion of epileptic spasms among dominant-negative variants (2 of 19 against 7 of 18, p 0.04) is called a possible chance finding given the number of associations tested.
entries.snippet: Given the large number of associations we examined, this could be a chance finding.

entries.proposition: Severe mobility and communication impairment are common regardless of variant function (56 and 64 percent), which the authors propose as trial endpoint domains.
entries.snippet: Our data highlight several potential areas, particularly mobility and communication, which may provide appropriate domains for trial endpoints as they are severely impaired in large proportions of patients regardless of variant function.

entries.proposition: The authors state that a heterologous-cell classification can miss trafficking and localisation defects and that severe disease can come with minimal measured channel impact (for example a variant with wild-type-like biophysics that disrupts a binding partner).
entries.snippet: severe clinical phenotypes can be associated with variants having minimal impact on heterologously expressed channels

entries.proposition: The authors say a prospective longitudinal study is needed to learn the effect of early effective seizure therapy on long-term development and to define the therapeutic window for disease-modifying interventions.
entries.snippet: A prospective longitudinal study will be valuable to ascertain the impact of early and effective anti‐seizure therapy on long‐term developmental outcomes in KCNQ2‐DEE

entries.proposition: Internal count check: the abstract gives 29 severe-loss, 13 loss, 3 gain and 2 wild-type-like participants (47 of 48), while Table 1 and the Results give 4 gain-of-function participants (29, 13, 2, 4 = 48).
entries.snippet: 1 variant (2 individuals) exhibited WTL properties, and 3 variants (4 individuals) were classified as GOF when expressed in the homozygous state
entries.anchor: Results, Functional properties of KCNQ2 variants

entries.proposition: Fig 2: stacked severity-score bars by functional class: gain-of-function (n=3 scored) at 0, 2 and 5, one third each; loss-of-function mostly scores 1 to 2 (50 percent at 1); severe loss spans 0 to 5; wild-type-like (n=2) all at 1. The classes do not share a common range: wild-type-like has only the score 1 and gain-of-function has no score 1.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 percent of participants by PSS: GOF 33 at PSS 0, 33 at PSS 2, 33 at PSS 5; LOF 8 at 0, 50 at 1, 17 at 2, 17 at 3, 8 at 4; SLOF 18 at 0, 27 at 1, 18 at 2, 18 at 3, 9 at 4, 9 at 5; WT-like 100 at 1.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Fig 2: stacked severity-score bars by functional class: gain-of-function (n=3 scored) from 0 to 5 with about one third at 5, loss-of-function mostly scores 1 to 2, severe loss spans 0 to 5, wild-type-like (n=2) all at 1; every class contains scores of 0 to 2. The original ended 'every class contains scores of 0 to 2', which is false: wild-type-like has only 1 and gain-of-function has no 1. The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: Fig 1: in the heterozygous state about 12 variants lie at 0.2 to 0.6 of wild-type peak current at plus 40 mV above the significance line and about five lie below it; activation midpoint shifts are within a few millivolts for most variants.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1A volcano: x peak current fold WT 0.2 to 0.8, blue significant points at about 0.25 to 0.45 with -log p about 3.4 (P335A, F305L, E140Q, G256R, H328N, D282N, W269S, S247L, F304S), A265V, D563N and T234P at 0.45 to 0.6 with -log p about 1.9 to 2.1; Fig 1B shifts of -8 to +2 mV with P335A about -7.7 mV.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (KCNQ2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, parent survey plus cell electrophysiology). Dataset S1 is titled 'Quantitative functional properties of KCNQ2 variants'.
entries.snippet: Dataset S1 - Quantitative functional properties of KCNQ2 variants

entries.proposition: The Figure S3 legend states that average whole-cell current densities at +40 mV from CHO-Q3 cells expressing epilepsy-associated KCNQ2 variants in the homozygous state are quantified relative to the wild-type channel measured in parallel.
entries.snippet: Average whole-cell current densities recorded at +40 mV from CHO-Q3 cells electroporated with epilepsy-associated KCNQ2 variants expressed in the homozygous state quantified relative to the WT channel measured in parallel (n = 10-77).

entries.proposition: Four variants (E123K, D212E, A235V, G301S) with more than 30 percent of wild-type current in the homozygous state were not tested in the heterozygous state, so the heterozygous series is selected by the homozygous result.
entries.snippet: Four variants (E123K, D212E, A235V, G301S) that had current densities greater than 30% of WT in the homozygous state were not tested in the heterozygous state.
entries.anchor: Figure S3 continued, legend C and D

entries.proposition: The supplement's severity-score key states that highlighted answers are scored 1 and all others 0.
entries.snippet: Highlighted answers are scored 1; all others are scored 0.

entries.proposition: The supplement states that data for R207W and T274M were previously published.
entries.snippet: Data for R207W and T274M were previously published.23

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure S4 (page 7): with 10 micromolar retigabine the heterozygous R207W and L292P curves rise above the wild-type curve, the D282N curve rises to about the wild-type level, and the T274M curve stays below the wild-type curve though above the untreated variant curve; four variants, with error bars on the points, no sample size printed and no statistics on the figure.

entries.anchor: Figure S4, read as an image

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure S5 (page 8): the phenotype severity score by age band (under 2, 2 to 4.9, 5 to 9.9, 10 and older) is a bar chart with individual points of about 8 to 12 per band, bars at about 1.2, 2.0, 2.3 and 2.0 on an axis that ends at 6 (the highest point is about 5); the bars are not labelled as means, so a difference of about one point between bands is read from bar heights; no test is shown.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure S3 panels A and B and C and D (pages 5 and 6): most variants sit well below 1.0 of wild-type peak current at +40 mV in the homozygous panels (A) and the heterozygous panels (C) with individual cells scattered up to 2 to 5 fold; in the activation-shift panels some variants (E123K and D212E in panel B, about +12 and +14 mV) are well away from zero, many are 'nd', and the heterozygous shifts (panel D) are mostly within a few millivolts of zero; the plots carry no statistics.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure S3 panels A-D list variants from E123K to R581G with open circles per cell, larger filled mean circles, dashed line at 1.0 and nd marks.
